steps.title: This is a learning machine.
steps.lede: StoryLab Voice turns one shared classroom tablet into a tutor, a library, and a science lab.
steps.text: It runs from this device. No signal. No laboratory. No account. The terminal remembers what you complete and keeps it ready for your teacher.
points: Three learning bays: stories, a voice tutor, and virtual experiments.
Every panel can be read aloud.
Everything is stored on this device.
steps.note: If the room goes quiet, the terminal still works.
steps.cue: This is your learning machine. Everything you need is on this device.

steps.title: Talk. It listens.
steps.lede: The amber SPEAK control opens the microphone. The waveform tells you what the terminal is doing.
steps.text: Amber means the tutor is speaking. Green means it is listening. If the room is too loud, move closer to the tablet and try again.
points: Wait for the green signal before you speak.
Speak in a normal voice, not a shout.
You can always tap an answer instead.
steps.note: Voice is the fastest way in. Touch is always there as a backup.
steps.cue: Press the amber control, wait for green, then speak. Touch is always available.

steps.title: Stories. A tutor. A lab.
steps.lede: Each bay teaches differently. They all feed the same learning record.
steps.text: StoryLearn narrates a branching story and asks you questions inside it. The AI Voice Tutor answers what you ask. LabInBox puts apparatus on screen and runs experiments with your voice.
points: BAY 02 — AI Voice Tutor: ask anything.
BAY 03 — Lab In Box: pour, react, observe.
steps.note: Start with a story if you are not sure where to begin.
steps.cue: Three bays. Stories, a voice tutor, and a virtual lab.

steps.title: Your work stays yours.
steps.lede: Progress is written to a local ledger on this device. No sign-in is required to learn.
steps.text: When the terminal finds a connection, queued records move to the sync archive. If there is no connection, nothing is lost — the queue simply waits.
points: Open RECORD to see sessions, checkpoints, and queued records.
Close a session before handing the tablet to the next student.
A facilitator can print or export the learning record.
steps.note: Sync is opportunistic. Learning is not.
steps.cue: Your progress is stored on this device. When a connection returns, the queue syncs.

steps.title: One question before we hand over the keys.
steps.lede: There is no time limit. Pick the answer that matches what the terminal does.
steps.question: Which control opens the microphone so you can talk to the tutor?

options.label: The amber SPEAK control
options.feedback: Correct. Amber is the action colour. Press SPEAK, wait for the green listening light, then talk.

options.label: The RECORD tab in the header
options.feedback: RECORD opens your learning file. The microphone lives on the amber SPEAK control.

options.label: The vent slots under the panel
options.feedback: Those are part of the chassis. Look for the amber SPEAK control instead.

steps.cue: One question. Which control opens the microphone?
